API_INTEGRATION_CARD.AUTHORIZATION_NOTE: The token your provider issued, as a bearer credential.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.EXAMPLE_HEADER_OPTI: {{header}} is not needed here, but it is accepted, so the request works as it stands.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.EXAMPLE_HEADER_REQU: {{header}} is required here, since another provider shares this issuer and audience.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.EXAMPLE_RESULT: A successful call returns the Blocks user the token mapped onto, through the claim mapping above.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.IDP_NOTE_REQUIRED: Required here: another active provider cannot be told apart from this one.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.INTRO: Every request carries the token and your project key. These are the headers.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.KEY_NOTE: Identifies the project the request belongs to. Always required.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.OPTIONAL_EXPLANATIO: The issuer and audience in the token already identify this provider, so {{header}} is not read and callers need not send it. It becomes necessary once another provider shares both — and because audience validation is off for any provider left without audiences, several such providers on one issuer are indistinguishable, which is the same case. Sending the header anyway is always accepted, and is the safer default if you expect to add more providers later.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.REQUIRED_EXPLANATIO: Another active provider shares this issuer and audience, so a token alone cannot say which of them it belongs to. Requests that omit {{header}} will be rejected. Giving the two providers different audiences removes the need for it.
API_INTEGRATION_CARD.TITLE: Calling the API with this provider's token

PROVIDER_DETAILS.CLAIM_MAPPING_HINT: Which claim of an incoming token supplies each field of the Blocks user.
PROVIDER_DETAILS.EXPIRED_WARNING: Tokens from this provider are being refused. Upload the replacement certificate to restore it.
PROVIDER_DETAILS.EXPIRING_WARNING: Ask the provider for the replacement before this date. A certificate pins a single key, so tokens stop being accepted the moment it lapses.
PROVIDER_DETAILS.SUBJECT: Subject
PROVIDER_DETAILS.UNREADABLE: The certificate could not be read when this provider was saved, so there is nothing to describe here. Check the URL above is reachable, then save the provider again.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.AUDIENCES_CONFLICT: Another active provider already uses this issuer. Give them different audiences, or neither can be told apart from the other and the caller chooses which mapping applies.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.AUDIENCES_HINT: Comma separated. Leaving this empty turns audience validation off, so any token from this issuer is accepted.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.CERTIFICATE_HINT: The provider's public certificate. Stored where token validation can read it back.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.DESCRIPTION: Tokens signed by this provider will be accepted on your APIs.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.ISSUERLESS_ALONE: Tokens carrying any issuer will not reach this provider.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.ISSUERLESS_SHARED: Another provider already accepts tokens without an issuer, so callers must send {{header}}: {{key}} to reach this one.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.ISSUER_HINT: Matched exactly against the token's iss, trailing slash included. Leave it empty only if this provider's tokens carry no iss at all — a blank issuer accepts those and nothing else.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.JWKS_HINT: Public keys, fetched over HTTPS. No secret is stored for this algorithm.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.JWKS_REQUIRED: A JWKS URL is required for this algorithm
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.KEY_CHARACTERS: Use letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore only
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.KEY_HINT_EDIT: A key is set. Leave this blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.KEY_HINT_NEW: The value callers send as {{header}}, if they ever need to.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.KEY_REQUIRED: Key is required — it is what the {{header}} header names
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.KEY_SOURCE_HINT: A JWKS survives the provider rotating a key; a certificate pins exactly one, so it has to be re-uploaded when they rotate. Prefer a JWKS wherever the provider publishes one — upload a certificate for an issuer that publishes none.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.PASSPHRASE_NOT_NEEDE: Not needed for this file — a .crt, .pem or .der holds only a public key, so there is nothing to unlock.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.PASSPHRASE_ONLY_PKCS: Only for a password-protected PKCS#12 (.pfx or .p12). Stored encrypted and never shown again.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.PASSPHRASE_PKCS12: This PKCS#12 file may be password protected. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.PASSPHRASE_STORED: A passphrase is stored. Leave this blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.SECRET_NEW: The shared secret your provider signs with. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.SECRET_STORED: A secret is stored. Leave this blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.STATUS_HINT: Tokens from an inactive provider are not accepted.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.STORED_REPLACE: {{label}}. Upload a file to replace it.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.STORE_FAILED: The certificate could not be stored, so nothing was saved.
PROVIDER_FORM_MODAL.UPLOAD_OR_JWKS: Upload a certificate, or switch this provider to a JWKS URL.

The discovery (well-known) URL below is generated for you — add the Client ID and Client Secret from that project's OIDC client registration, and the redirect URI your app should receive the callback on.
